title: juried-eval-weighting-and-uncertainty-calibration
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Establish a revised benchmarking and scoring methodology that combines juried rubric weighting with calibrated LLM-as-judge confidence scores, stratified cohort baselines, and clearer service-level triggers for config/model changes. Goal is to reduce noisy regression alerts, surface actionable degradations, and enable safe automated mitigations (canary, rollback) without increasing false positives.

Problem: Current eval signals are brittle across model variants and config changes (quantization, KV cache policies, batching). We receive noisy regression alerts when non-impactful config changes alter tokenization or output formatting. This causes churn in rollouts and reduces trust in automatic gating.

Proposal: 1) Define a juried rubric per cohort that weights dimensions (semantic fidelity, safety, formatting, latency-sensitive correctness). 2) Use an LLM-as-judge ensemble to score samples, then calibrate those scores to true human agreement scores using isotonic regression per-cohort. 3) Compute cohort-level delta metrics with uncertainty intervals; only surface alerts when the calibrated effect size exceeds a cohort-specific threshold and is supported by multiple judge models or human spot-checks. 4) Add a labeled metadata layer so config change records (e.g., quantization, kernel selection, kv-cache-policy) are associated with eval runs to enable attribution.

Why now: Increasing use of aggressive quantization + new kernel paths in runtime-1.20 caused several noisy regressions during Dedicated and Private rollouts. We need higher-fidelity decision signals to reduce rollback churn and allow fast safe rollouts.

Trade-offs: - More compute and storage for ensemble judge runs and calibration pipelines. - Complexity in maintaining per-cohort calibration models (data drift requires retraining cadence). - Risk of LLM-judge bias on subjective rubric items; mitigations below.
acceptance_criteria: Rubric document published in Confluence with numeric weights per cohort and examples
LLM-as-judge ensemble implemented in eval harness and runs nightly against targeted cohorts
Isotonic calibration pipeline implemented; per-cohort calibration models trained and versioned
Dashboard shows calibrated score deltas, uncertainty intervals, and top-attributed config keys
Automated alerting rule: signal must exceed cohort threshold and be observed by >=2 judge models or include human spot-check failure
Canary rollout integration: failing canaries mark rollout paused and create a PM/ENG incident ticket
testing_plan: Unit tests for calibration code and score aggregation
Synthetic adversarial harness to validate robustness to formatting changes
Canary run on Dedicated staging with two model variants across three cohorts
Human audit: random sample of 200 adjudicated items across cohorts with inter-annotator agreement > 0.7
Backtest on prior 6 months of eval runs to verify reduction in noisy alerts by >=30%
rollout_plan: Phase 1: publish rubric + run offline calibration on historical data (2 weeks). Phase 2: nightly ensemble runs and dashboarding in read-only mode (3 weeks). Phase 3: enable advisory alerts to on-call (2 weeks). Phase 4: enable automated canary pause + PM review gating for Dedicated (4 weeks).
decision_log: 2026-02-25: Decided to use isotonic regression for calibration because we expect non-linear score->prob mappings and want monotonicity preserved
2026-03-02: Chose ensemble of 3 judge models (base, temperature-varied, safety-tuned) instead of single judge to reduce model-specific bias
2026-03-08: Thresholds will be cohort-specific and derived from historical variance + business impact weighting rather than a global p-value
updates: 2026-02-20 - Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after postmortem on noisy rollouts. Draft rubric examples attached.
2026-02-26 - ML Research (Lina Zhou): Reviewed proposal; recommended ensemble judges and flagged potential bias on 'helpfulness' rubric—recommended adding explicit guideline anchors
2026-03-03 - Engineering (Miguel Ortega): Identified runtime telemetry dependency ENG-2345 for attributing kv-cache and kernel changes. Estimate updated to 3 points.
2026-03-05 - Design (Rory Bennett): Provided annotation UI wireframes for human spot-check workflow and disagreement resolution
2026-03-10 - PM sync: Agreed on isotonic regression calibration and cadence: weekly retrain for cohorts with >10k samples per month, monthly otherwise
2026-03-12 - Security review request submitted (low risk); no blocking items identified
notes: Mitigations for judge bias: mandatory human spot-checks on first three runs after a config change; adversarial test-set that targets known LLM failure modes; periodic A/B comparisons vs human majority vote. Long-term: explore mixed-effects hierarchical calibration to share signal across low-data cohorts.
